units.title: Look forward to
units.grammar_focus: 3-part phrasal verbs with -ing (look forward to, get used to, object to)
units.real_life_context: You express anticipation, adaptation, or objection — all followed by -ing.

grammar.sentence: I look forward _____ you next week.
grammar.explanation: "Look forward to" é phrasal verb + preposição "to" + -ING. Erro comum: usar "to see" (base form). Sempre "to + verb-ing" após "look forward to".
"Get used to + -ing" — adaptação. "To waking up" — preposição "to" + gerúndio.
"Object to + -ing" — oposição/recusa. "To smoking" — gerúndio obrigatório.
"Look forward to going" — antecipação positiva com -ing.
"Used to living" — habituado. Note: difere de "used to live" (costumava) — pista é o "TO + -ing" não "TO + base".
"Object to working" — oposição. Sempre "to + -ing".
"Look forward to hearing" — fórmula formal em emails. Comum em encerramento.

grammar.sentence: I look forward to see you tomorrow.
grammar.hint: Após "to" em look forward to, gerúndio
grammar.answer: I look forward to seeing you tomorrow.
grammar.explanation: Erro super comum. "Look forward to" — preposição "to" + -ING, não base form. "To seeing", não "to see".

grammar.sentence: She's getting used to wake up early.
grammar.hint: Após "to" em get used to, gerúndio
grammar.answer: She's getting used to waking up early.
grammar.explanation: "Get used to + -ing". "To wake up" só funciona em "used to wake up" (costumava acordar). Aqui é adaptação atual.

grammar.passage: I look forward to seeing you next week. She's getting used to waking up early for work. He objects to smoking in restaurants. We look forward to hearing from you soon.
grammar.question: What is she getting used to?
grammar.answer: waking up early (or "waking up early for work")
grammar.explanation: The text says "She's getting used to waking up early for work".

listening_speaking.text: I look forward to seeing you.
I'm getting used to working from home.
She objects to smoking in restaurants.
We look forward to hearing from you.
I'm not used to driving in the city.

units.title: Put up with
units.grammar_focus: 3-part phrasal verbs of tolerance/depletion (put up with, run out of, get away with)
units.real_life_context: You describe tolerating, running out, or escaping consequences.

grammar.explanation: "Put up with" = tolerar. 3-part phrasal: put + up + with. Sempre nessa ordem.
"Run out of + noun" = ficar sem. "Ran out of milk" — esgotamos o leite.
"Get away with + noun/-ing" = escapar das consequências. "Gets away with lies".
"Put up with noise" — tolerar barulho. Reclamação.
"Ran out of time" — chunk muito comum, falta de tempo.
"How do you put up with" — pergunta sobre tolerância.
"Won't get away with cheating" — não vai escapar.

grammar.sentence: I can't put with this noise.
grammar.answer: I can't put up with this noise.
grammar.explanation: "Put with" não existe. Sempre 3 partes: "put + UP + with".
"Run out OF + noun" — preposição "of" obrigatória. "Running out" sozinho não funciona com objeto.

grammar.passage: I can't put up with his attitude anymore. We ran out of milk this morning. He always gets away with breaking the rules. How do you put up with that smell?
grammar.question: What do they need to buy?
grammar.explanation: The text says "We ran out of milk this morning".

units.title: Get along with
units.grammar_focus: 3-part phrasals about relationships (get along with, look up to, look down on, get on with)
units.real_life_context: You describe how you relate to other people.

grammar.explanation: "Get along with + person" = relacionar-se bem. Phrasal de relacionamento harmonioso.
"Look up to + person" = admirar. Imagina olhar para cima com respeito.
"Look down on + person" = desprezar. Oposto de "look up to".
"Don't get along with each other" — relação ruim. Sempre com "with".

grammar.sentence: I really _____ my old boss — she was inspiring.
grammar.explanation: "Look up to" — admirar como modelo.
"Hard to get along with" — difícil de conviver.

grammar.sentence: She _____ poor people, which is awful.
grammar.explanation: "Looks down on poor people" — comportamento criticável de desprezo.

grammar.answer: I get along with my coworkers.
grammar.explanation: "Get along" sozinho funciona ("we get along well"), mas com pessoa específica precisa "with".

grammar.answer: She looks up to her grandfather.
grammar.explanation: "Look up to" — 3 partes obrigatórias. Sem "to" significa "olhar para cima fisicamente".

grammar.passage: I get along with my coworkers really well. She looks up to her grandfather as a role model. He unfortunately looks down on people without degrees. We don't always get along with each other.
grammar.question: Whom does she look up to?
grammar.explanation: The text says "She looks up to her grandfather as a role model".

listening_speaking.text: I get along with my coworkers.

units.title: Catch up, make up
units.grammar_focus: Phrasals of time, compensation, commitment (catch up with, make up for, keep up with, go through with)
units.real_life_context: You handle deadlines, debts, news, and commitments.

grammar.explanation: "Catch up ON + thing/topic" para colocar em dia com algo. "Catch up on emails" = atualizar-se com os emails.
"Catch up" sozinho = se ver/falar para atualizar. "Let's catch up" — combinar de conversar.
"Make up for + noun" = compensar. "Make up for the mistake" — compensar o erro.

grammar.sentence: It's hard to _____ all the changes.
grammar.explanation: "Keep up with + thing" = manter o ritmo, acompanhar. "Keep up with changes".

grammar.sentence: I'll _____ the plan despite the doubts.
grammar.explanation: "Go through with + plan/decision" = levar adiante. Apesar de dúvidas.
"Catch up on the news" — atualizar-se sobre notícias.

grammar.sentence: Sorry for being late — I'll _____ it tomorrow.
grammar.explanation: "Make up for it tomorrow" — compensar a falta.

grammar.sentence: I need to catch up my emails.
grammar.answer: I need to catch up on my emails.
grammar.explanation: "Catch up" precisa de preposição quando há objeto. "On" para coisas/temas, "with" para pessoas.

grammar.sentence: Let's catch up with on the project.
grammar.answer: Let's catch up on the project.
grammar.explanation: "Catch up on" para tema/objeto. "With" só para pessoas. Não pode misturar.

grammar.passage: I need to catch up on my emails. Let's catch up next week! I want to make up for my mistake. It's hard to keep up with all the changes. I'll go through with the plan.
grammar.question: What do they need to do with their emails?
grammar.answer: catch up on them (or "catch up on the emails")
grammar.explanation: The text says "I need to catch up on my emails".

Let's catch up next week.

units.title: Idiomatic chunks
units.grammar_focus: High-frequency idiomatic chunks (on second thought, at the end of the day, in the long run, for the time being)
units.real_life_context: You use natural conversational chunks for emphasis, qualification, or summary.

grammar.explanation: "On second thought" = pensando melhor. Chunk fixo de reconsideração. Não é "at" ou "in".

options: At the end of the day
In the end of the day
grammar.answer: At the end of the day
grammar.explanation: "At the end of the day" = no fim das contas/em última análise. Chunk de conclusão filosófica. Não é "in".
"In the long run" = a longo prazo. Chunk para perspectiva temporal estendida.
"For the time being" = por enquanto, temporariamente.

grammar.sentence: _____, the project is fine — let's move on.
grammar.hint: By and large (no geral, em sua maioria)
grammar.explanation: "By and large" = de modo geral. Chunk para resumo qualificado.
"On second thought" — reconsideração. Mudou de ideia.

grammar.sentence: _____, exercise is what makes the difference.
grammar.explanation: "In the long run" — perspectiva de longo prazo.

grammar.sentence: In the end of the day, it doesn't matter.
grammar.answer: At the end of the day, it doesn't matter.
grammar.explanation: Chunk fixo: "AT the end of the day". "In the end" funciona como variante mas "at the end of the day" é o chunk idiomático.
Chunk fixo: "ON second thought". Outras preposições não funcionam.

grammar.passage: On second thought, let's go tomorrow instead. At the end of the day, what matters is being happy. In the long run, the investment will pay off. For the time being, I'll keep working from home.
grammar.question: What investment outlook does the speaker take?
grammar.answer: long run (or "in the long run" or "long-term")
grammar.explanation: The text says "In the long run, the investment will pay off".

listening_speaking.text: On second thought, let's wait.
At the end of the day, family matters most.
In the long run, it'll be worth it.
For the time being, this works.
By and large, it's fine.

cross_unit_consolidation: Look forward to / get used to / object to + -ING (preposição "to" + gerúndio)
Put up with / run out of / get away with (tolerar, esgotar, escapar)
Get along with / look up to / look down on (relacionamentos)
Catch up on (coisa) / catch up with (pessoa) / make up for / keep up with / go through with
Chunks idiomáticos: on second thought, at the end of the day, in the long run, for the time being, by and large
